t: Khartoum was founded in 1821 as an Egyptian army outpost and became the seat of the colonial government in 1823, a trading town on the caravan route from Ethiopia to Egypt and a focal point of the slave trade.

Mahdist forces besieged it from 13 March 1884 and took it on 26 January 1885, after which it was largely destroyed and abandoned, and Anglo-Egyptian forces refounded it as a capital after the reconquest of 1898.

It became the capital of independent Sudan in 1956, grew from 185,000 people in 1964 to an estimated 7.1 million in Greater Khartoum, and saw extensive fighting between the armed forces and the Rapid Support Forces from 2023.
dyk: After the Mahdists took Khartoum in 1885 the survivors were deported to the newly established Omdurman, and when the city was rebuilt after 1898 its street plan was laid out in the shape of the Union Jack.
ev: Isma'il Kamil Pasha establishes Khartoum as an outpost of the Egyptian Army
Egypt moves the seat of its colonial government from Wad Madani to Khartoum
Heavy rains and floods destroy most of the city, which is rebuilt in mud and stone
The Mahdists take Khartoum after a siege that began in 1884, and the garrison is annihilated
Anglo-Egyptian forces reoccupy the city, which becomes the capital of Anglo-Egyptian Sudan
Khartoum becomes the capital of independent Sudan
Fighting between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces begins in the city

f.founded: Established in 1821, 24 km north of the ancient city of Soba, by Isma'il Kamil Pasha, third son of Egypt's ruler Muhammad Ali Pasha, as an outpost for the Egyptian Army.
f.where: At the confluence of the Blue Nile and the White Nile in central Sudan, at an elevation of 385 m, with Khartoum North and Omdurman across the rivers.
f.known: The Egyptian colonial capital from 1823; a centre of caravan trade and the slave trade; the siege of 1884 to 1885 and the death of General Gordon; the Anglo-Egyptian capital rebuilt after 1898; the capital of independent Sudan from 1956
f.today: Khartoum is the capital of Sudan and of Khartoum State, and with Khartoum North and Omdurman forms the country's largest urban area.
